parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aina (compare Estonian aina), probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic [Term?] (compare Old Prussian ainat (“always, constantly”) and Lithuanian vienàt (“only”)).

From Proto-Finnic *ansa (compare Estonian aas), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ansā (compare Old Prussian ansis (“hook, latch”), Latvian osa), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂emseh₂ (compare Latin ānsa (“handle”)).

parole.significato: tooth (hard, calcareous structure present in the mouth of many vertebrate animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hambas (compare Estonian hammas), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źámbas (replacing native Uralic pii < *piŋe; compare Proto-Slavic *zǫbъ, Lithuanian žam̃bas, Latvian zòbs), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵómbʰos. Doublet of kampa.

From Proto-Finnic *hanhi (compare Estonian hani), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źansís (compare Lithuanian žąsis). Compare Erzya шенже (šenže, “duck”), which was probably borrowed from the same Balto-Slavic source.

parole.significato: hay (grass cut and dried for use as animal fodder)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haina (compare Estonian hein, Võro hain), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *śaina- (compare Lithuanian šienas, Proto-Slavic *sěno).

parole.significato: pea (plant, Pisum sativum, syn. Lathyrus oleraceus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *herneh (compare Estonian hernes), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źírˀnan (compare Lithuanian žirnis).

parole.significato: already (prior to some time; so soon)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jo (compare Estonian ju, Ingrian jo, Karelian jo, Livonian jo, Veps jo, Votic jo), probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *jau (*iou) (compare Latvian jau, Lithuanian jaũ). parole.significato: spot, location (especially a more exact location of or within something else)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kokta (compare Estonian koht), probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *kokto (compare Latvian kakts (“corner, nook”), Lithuanian kakta (“forehead”)).

parole.significato: an intensifier; corresponds to the English auxiliary do in many cases
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küllä (compare Estonian küll, Ingrian kyl, Livonian ki’l), from earlier *küllä (compare Northern Sami galˈle), probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *k⁽ʷ⁾el- (compare Lithuanian keli̇̀ (“how many, some, few, several”)). From Proto-Finnic *oinas, borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *awinas (compare Lithuanian ãvinas, Latvian auns).

parole.significato: A traditional thin unleavened bread made from barley, oats and/or potato.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rëëska, borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *prḗˀskas (compare Lithuanian prėskas (“unflavoured, tasteless, fresh, unleavened”)).
From Proto-Finnic *sisar, borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *swésō or Proto-Indo-European *swésōr (compare Erzya сазор (sazor)).

parole.significato: A (coarse) brush, especially one used for brushing animals, such as a currycomb for grooming horses.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *suka, probably borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic [Term?] (compare Latvian suka).

parole.significato: The meaning of this term is uncertain. Possibilities include:
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tarvas, borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *taurás, from Proto-Indo-European *táwros. Doublet of Taurus, teuras, and torvi.
From Proto-Finnic *tühjä (compare Estonian tühi), borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *tuskjas (compare Lithuanian tuščias (“empty”), Latvian tukšs (“empty, blank”)).

From Proto-Finnic *virci, from earlier *virti, borrowed from Proto-Balto-Slavic *wirdas (compare Latvian vārds (“word, name”) and Old Prussian wīrds), from Proto-Indo-European *werdʰom (compare English word, Latin verbum). Doublet of verbi.
